en.title: Ash, the Beginning
paras: Ash was born on a stormy night, in a small village just beyond the walls of Nyfurion’s castle. His parents, cloaked in mystery, brought him to the castle gates and vanished without a trace. No one ever saw their faces. Rumor had it they died shortly after his birth, leaving him alone in the world. Whispers claimed Ash was the last heir of an ancient and enigmatic bloodline, rich in hidden power.

Raised in the shadows of the royal halls, Ash quickly learned to rely only on himself. Those around him treated him with respect, but always at a distanceas if his solitude were contagious. His childhood was quiet, filled with fleeting glances and unspoken words. No one truly cared for him, yet Ash never complained. He watched, he learned, he listened.

The castle was a place of shadows and secrets, with endless corridors and rooms filled with ancient relics. Ash wandered silently, mastering the art of moving unnoticed, catching fragments of conversations and details that escaped the adults. At night, he often stood by the tower windows, gazing at the stars, wondering if someone, somewhere, was thinking of him.

He found refuge among the books of the castle’s grand library and the stories of those who lived within its walls. He spent hours immersed in tales of brave kings, powerful sorcerers, and ancient wars. Those pages became his friends and mentors. He taught himself to read, deciphering letters and symbols, and soon the library became his secret kingdom. But the company of books wasn’t enough. Often, in secret, he would leave the castle to visit the villages surrounding Nyfurion. There, he learned to understand the people of the realm listening to elders’ stories, playing with children, observing merchants and farmers in their daily struggles. No one knew that the kind, curious boy was destined to become the future king. Not even Ash could have imagined it.

One day, during one of his forest explorations, Ash heard a rustle in the bushes. He approached cautiously, ready to flee, but found himself face to face with an old man—his face weathered, his eyes deep and intense. The man introduced himself as Lexy. His voice was hoarse, yet carried an authority that demanded respect.

Lexy invited him into his modest dwelling a hidden hut among the trees, its walls covered in ancient symbols and strange artifacts. The air was thick with mystery, and Ash instantly sensed that this man was no ordinary hermit. Lexy began to speak of Nyfurion’s protective relics: magical objects hidden in the kingdom’s most remote places, capable of repelling dark forces and preserving peace. With a slow gesture, he pulled from beneath his robe an ancient medallion engraved with mysterious symbols.

Ash was breathless. Lexy explained that the medallion was one of the kingdom’s relics. “Every king of Nyfurion,” Lexy said gravely, “is charged with protecting these relics even at the cost of their own life. But the hunger for power can corrupt even the purest hearts.”

Ash listened, captivated yet unsettled. For the first time, he felt part of something far greater than himself a millennia-old tale of secrets, sacrifice, and forgotten magic. But he also sensed the danger that loomed over the relics and those who guarded them. Lexy’s stories ignited in him a spark of curiosity and fear that would never fade.

That night, returning to the castle, Ash felt a new resolve awaken within him. He would not let solitude define him. He would uncover every mystery of Nyfurion, protect its people, and honor the memory of a family he never knew. From that day on, the orphaned boy began to grow faster, driven by the desire to find his place in the world—and by the suspicion that his fate was entwined with Lexy’s and the medallion’s.

en.title: The Awakening
paras: The years passed quietly within the walls of Nyfurion’s castle. Ash, now a teenager, had changed: the lonely child had become a sharp-eyed young man, restless in spirit and driven by a growing desire to uncover his origins a fire within him that refused to die.

Questions crowded his mind: Who were his parents, truly? Why had they left him at the castle gates? And why did no one seem willing to speak of his past? The more he searched for answers in the castle’s corridors, the more he encountered silence and evasive glances. At times, Ash felt as though everyone knew something he didn’t and that made him feel even more alone.

Only Lexy seemed willing to share fragments of truth. Ash often visited the old man’s hut at the edge of the forest, where the air smelled of moss and mystery. Lexy taught him to read ancient symbols, to recognize the marks left by time on stones and trees, to sense the invisible magic flowing through the kingdom. In those hours, Ash felt truly seen as if Lexy perceived something in him that no one else could. Ash listened intently to every word, every tale about Nyfurion’s relics. He sensed that behind those stories lay something vital, perhaps the key to understanding his destiny. But Lexy was skilled at changing the subject when Ash’s questions became too direct, leaving him with a growing frustration and an even deeper curiosity. Sometimes, the old man would fall silent mid-sentence, as if afraid of revealing too much, and his gaze would suddenly darken.

As the months passed, Ash realized he was changing on the inside too. A new strength was awakening within him a heightened sensitivity to the world around him. His dreams grew more vivid, filled with symbols and visions from ancient times. He often woke in the middle of the night, heart pounding, convinced he had glimpsed answers in his sleep. Each night, before drifting off, he promised himself that one day he would uncover the full truth about his origins and the mystery surrounding Nyfurion’s relics.

During the day, Ash continued to move between the castle halls and the surrounding villages. In the castle, he observed carefully, trying to catch fragments of conversations that might reveal something about his past. He often retreated to the library, poring over dusty old tomes in search of symbols like those Lexy had shown him. He began to notice details he’d missed before: a medallion like Lexy’s in an ancient fresco, a phrase in an unknown language carved into a column, a hidden symbol tucked between the pages of an old book.

One evening, while in the map room, Ash noticed a candle flame flicker strangely as he passed. He stopped, intrigued, and reached toward the light. Without knowing how, the flame stretched toward him, dancing in the air as if responding to his presence. Ash pulled his hand back, startled, heart racing. No one seemed to notice but he knew something extraordinary had just occurred.
The next day, he returned to Lexy in the forest, determined to share what had happened. The old man greeted him with a watchful gaze.
“Lexy, yesterday… something strange happened. A candle it moved toward me. I didn’t touch it, but it was like it heard me.”

Lexy paused for a moment, then offered a faint smile. “Do not fear, Ash. The ancient blood within you is beginning to awaken. The stories I tell you are not merely echoes of the past they are keys to unlock doors within yourself.”
Ash stared at him, confused and fascinated. “What do you mean, Lexy?”
Lexy replied, “Your powers belong only to those who bear the mark of Nyfurion’s dynasty. Your strength is still raw, but it will grow. You must learn to listen to it.”

From that day on, Ash began to train in secret. He practiced moving small objects, sensing the presence of people without seeing them, feeling the heartbeat of nature around him. Each time he succeeded even for a moment he felt a deep joy and a subtle fear. He knew these powers made him different, but also that they were the key to discovering who he truly was.

In the castle, his movements became more deliberate. He studied the symbols carved into doors, the ancient armor lining the corridors, the paintings of kings and queens with stern faces. He began to notice details he’d once overlooked: a medallion like Lexy’s in a faded fresco, a phrase in an unknown tongue etched into a column.
One evening, as Lexy showed him an ancient manuscript, Ash asked, “Why does no one ever speak of the relics? Why does everyone seem afraid of these stories?”

Lexy looked at him for a long moment, then answered in a low voice, “Because power, Ash, frightens those who do not understand it. And those who crave it are often willing to do anything to possess it. You must be different. You must learn to know your strength but also to protect it.”

Those words etched themselves into Ash’s mind. From that moment on, each day became a discovery of himself, of the kingdom, and of the secrets that surrounded him. And each night, in his dreams, Lexy’s voice and the call of the relics grew stronger and more urgent.

en.title: Bonds and Power
paras: As the years passed, the bond between Ash and Lexy grew ever stronger. What had begun as mere curiosity had deepened into something profound built on trust, respect, and affection. Lexy had become Ash’s confidant, his guide, and perhaps the father figure he had never known. And Ash, in turn, brought a new light into Lexy’s life a hope the old man had long thought lost.

Lexy, who had once known both glory and disgrace within the castle walls, saw in Ash a chance for redemption. Day after day, in their secret meetings, Lexy shared stories of ancient magic and the relics of Nyfurion. Ash listened intently, absorbing every word, every gesture, every tale Lexy passed on with patience and care. Between them, a language had formed one of glances and silences, of small gestures that spoke louder than words.

Ash’s power grew alongside their bond. His abilities sharpened: he could sense people from far away, hear their deepest thoughts, influence wind and rain with sheer will. Lexy urged him to push his limits. “Listen to the breath of the forest, Ash. Feel how magic flows beneath the bark of the trees, through the roots and leaves.” Ash would close his eyes and let the world around him transform into a mosaic of ancient energies and forgotten sounds.

But with growth came new challenges. The stronger his magic became, the harder it was to contain. A surge of emotion anger, fear, sorrow could trigger inexplicable phenomena: a sudden storm, a flash of light in his hands, a whisper that made the earth tremble. One night, overwhelmed by anxiety, Ash unintentionally withered every rose in the royal garden.

At the castle, no one suspected a thing. Ash had learned to hide every trace of his powers, to behave like any other quiet, respectful young man. The nobles saw him as reserved perhaps a little strange but nothing more. Only Lexy knew the truth: behind that mask was the future of Nyfurion, the heir to an ancient bloodline, destined to reshape the kingdom’s fate.

Ash trusted Lexy completely. He had nothing to fear or so he believed. He could not imagine that behind the mask of affection and wisdom lay a darker plan. Lexy needed him. He knew Ash descended from a powerful family the last survivor after the bloodline was wiped out in a surprise attack. Only Lexy had seen the truth, recognizing in Ash the signs of royal lineage. That was why he had drawn close to him, binding him tightly, guiding him step by step toward the discovery of his hidden power.

But Lexy’s true purpose was far from what Ash could have imagined: he intended to use the boy’s strength for revenge to destroy Nyfurion and punish the kingdom that had exiled him. And while Ash surrendered to trust, unaware, the fate of Nyfurion crept ever closer to a dark turning point.

en.title: An Unexpected Encounter
paras: It was a clear evening as Ash made his way back to the castle after one of his usual meetings with Lexy. His mind was still full of thoughts and questions, his steps quick along the paths that cut through the forest and meadows. The air smelled of damp earth and leaves, and the birdsong mingled with the rustling wind in the branches. He expected nothing unusual from the day yet fate had a surprise in store.

As he walked alongside a small stream, Ash heard a rustle in the bushes. Before he could turn, something or rather, someone collided with him, nearly knocking him over. A startled exclamation, then a crystalline laugh: “Oh, sorry! I didn’t see you!”

Ash found himself on the ground, still dazed. In front of him, a girl with copper-colored hair had gotten her dress tangled in the branches. She tried to free herself, but the more she struggled, the more comical the situation became. Ash, still a bit stunned, couldn’t help but laugh.

“Let me help you,” he said, offering his hand. The girl accepted, but as she tried to stand, she slipped again, pulling Ash down with her. The two ended up sitting in the grass, side by side, cheeks flushed from laughter.
“My name’s Mary,” she said, still catching her breath. “And you must be Ash, right? I’ve heard about you at the castle… though I didn’t expect you to be so… um, agile!”
Ash laughed, feeling a lightness he hadn’t felt in a long time. “I’m usually more careful, but today fate decided to test me.”
Mary smiled, her gaze shining with a light all its own. “Then we’re both in the same boat. I’m new around here too. Got lost in the paths and… well, you know the rest.”

They stood up together, still laughing, and Ash offered to walk her back to the castle. They strolled side by side, exchanging jokes and stories as if they’d known each other forever. Mary spoke of how she had recently moved to Nyfurion, how she found the woods enchanting and the castle’s ancient walls mysterious. Ash, in turn, told her about his favorite places, the nights spent watching stars from the highest towers, and the stories he’d learned from the village elders.

With each step, the conversation grew more natural. Mary had a contagious laugh and a way of seeing the world that intrigued Ash. “You know,” she said at one point, “I think the best things happen when you get lost. Like today.”
Ash nodded, feeling a strange happiness rise within him. “Maybe fate made us stumble into each other for a reason.”

As they crossed a small wooden bridge, Mary paused to look at the sunset’s reflection on the water. “I didn’t expect Nyfurion to be so beautiful. Maybe, with the right company, everything feels more magical.”
Ash watched her in silence, struck by her sincerity. “Sometimes it takes very little to change a day. Or maybe an entire life.”

By the time they reached the castle gates, the sun was low on the horizon and the towers cast long shadows across the fields. Before parting, Mary turned to Ash and smiled once more. “I hope I get lost again maybe with you next time.”

Ash watched her walk away, his heart light and his mind full of new questions. That encounter, born of chance and a small accident, marked the beginning of something special a spark that would forever alter both their destinies. And as the sun set behind Nyfurion’s towers, Ash felt, for the first time, that the future no longer frightened him.

en.title: Shadows Between Feelings
paras: After their first encounter, Ash and Mary began seeing each other more and more often. At first, it was just chance meetings in the castle gardens, strolls through the village alleys, or quiet conversations beneath the stars. Mary brought a lightness into Ash’s life that he had never known before with her, he laughed, opened up, and finally felt free to be himself. With each passing day, their bond grew deeper, and Ash found himself longing more and more for her presence.

Over time, their meetings became a cherished ritual. Mary was the only one who could make Ash forget the weight of his responsibilities and the shadows that followed him. Together, they explored hidden corners of the kingdom, shared dreams and fears, and between them blossomed a sincere connection built on small gestures and knowing glances. Ash felt truly alive, as if beside Mary he could finally be the boy he had always wished to be.

Their days were filled with laughter and confidences, with spontaneous games in the courtyards and long conversations under the moonlight. Mary had a gift for sensing Ash’s thoughts even when he remained silent, and often a single look was enough to understand each other. Ash, in turn, found himself sharing secrets he had never told anyone not even himself.

And yet, despite the happiness Mary gave him, Ash couldn’t escape Lexy’s influence. The old man continued to meet with him, spinning tales of vengeance and power, pushing him toward a destiny that felt heavier with each passing day. Lexy was skilled at weaving truth with lies, exploiting Ash’s insecurities and his longing to uncover his origins. Every time Ash returned from one of these meetings, he felt a strange unease inside him as if a part of him was drifting away from the light Mary had brought into his life.

As the years went by, Mary began to notice changes in Ash. His gaze grew darker, his silences longer. She often found him lost in thought, distant even when he was right beside her. Ash was becoming more powerful but also more troubled, as if an inner battle was consuming him day by day. Sometimes, during their walks, Mary would see him staring into nothingness, fists clenched, as if fighting an invisible war.

Mary tried to reach him, to pull him back to reality, but Ash seemed to slip away trapped by a promise he had made to himself and to Lexy. “Ash, what’s tormenting you?” she would ask at times, but he would only offer a faint smile, change the subject, or retreat into silence.

One day, during a storm, Mary found Ash in the forest, kneeling before an ancient tree, his hands trembling with energy. Lightning lit up the sky and rain poured down, but Mary didn’t hesitate. She knelt beside him, unfazed by the mud and cold, and took his hands in hers. “Ash, what’s happening to you?” she whispered, her voice trembling with worry.

Ash looked at her with eyes full of pain and confusion, unable to find the words. He felt the magic boiling inside him, out of control, as if something dark was trying to take over. “I don’t know, Mary… I feel like I’m losing myself. I’m afraid of what I’m becoming.”

Mary held him tightly, wrapping him in an embrace as if trying to shield him from the entire world. “You’re not alone, Ash. I’m here. Don’t let the darkness take you. Whatever happens, we’ll fight together.”

In that moment, Mary understood that something dark was growing inside him and that only the truth could save him. She resolved to do whatever it took to bring Ash back to the light, even if it meant facing the shadows that threatened to tear them apart forever.

en.title: The Truth Revealed
paras: The kingdom of Nyfurion seemed wrapped in an eerie calm. Days passed quietly within the castle walls, yet Mary sensed a subtle unease drifting through the air. Ash had changed his eyes, once full of curiosity, now often stared into nothingness. He wandered the corridors with a tense expression, fists clenched, as if fighting an invisible war.

Mary watched him from afar, her heart tight with worry. She saw him gaze silently into the fireplace, or roam the halls at night, unable to sleep. Every time she tried to ask what tormented him, Ash withdrew into stubborn silence, avoiding her gaze.
Mary Begins to Investigate

One night, unable to bear the anguish any longer, Mary decided to act. She waited until the castle had fallen into silence, then slipped into the secret archives. Her fingers trembled as she flipped through ancient volumes, candlelight casting dancing shadows on the walls. Among the yellowed pages, she found familiar symbols the same ones she had seen in Ash’s dreams.

An old librarian caught her between the shelves. “Seeking answers, my lady?” Mary nodded, hesitant. “Tell me about Lexy. What is he hiding from his past?” The man lowered his gaze. “Lexy was exiled years ago. He sought power in forbidden relics. He was obsessed… and those who followed him paid dearly for his ambition.”

Mary thanked him with a nod and continued her search, listening to the whispers of an elderly woman who remembered the time of exile: “Lexy had stormy eyes and honeyed words. But his heart… his heart already belonged to the shadows.”
Discoveries and Suspicions

Digging through scrolls, Mary found a worn diary. Its pages told of a young Lexy brilliant, ambitious who had betrayed the kingdom’s trust in his thirst for power. In a flash, she saw the image of Lexy clutching a relic in his hands, his face twisted by greed.
Mary shuddered. It all made sense now: the symbols, the stories, Ash’s transformation. Lexy was the source of the darkness consuming the boy she loved.

That evening, Mary waited for Ash in the library, among the shadows of ancient shelves. Rain lashed against the windows, and the wind made the candles tremble. “Ash, we need to talk,” she said firmly, holding out the diary.

Ash looked at her, confused and defensive. “What is all this?” “It’s the truth about Lexy. He’s using you, Ash. He only wants to destroy the kingdom of Nyfurion. You are so much more than what he wants you to believe.”

Ash clenched his fists, his voice breaking. “Lexy has always protected me. He taught me everything. This can’t be true…” Mary stepped closer, her eyes filled with tears. “Can’t you see how much you’ve changed? You’re not yourself anymore. He’s pulling you away from me, from who you are.”
Ash turned away, torn between loyalty and doubt. “You don’t understand… I owe him everything.” “You don’t owe him your soul, Ash. You have to choose who you want to be.”
Ash ran off, heart in turmoil, but Mary’s words echoed in his mind like thunder.
Ash Discovers the Truth

That night, unable to find peace, Ash decided to follow Lexy. He moved silently through the village shadows, slipping past the castle walls and into the forest surrounding Nyfurion. His heart pounded as he hid among the trees, tracking the old man’s steps.
In a hidden clearing, lit only by the flickering glow of lanterns, Ash saw Lexy surrounded by armed men. Their voices were low, thick with hatred and hunger for power.
“Soon the kingdom will fall,” Lexy whispered to his followers. “Ash will do what he must. No one will suspect him until the time is right. Then Nyfurion will be ours.”
Ash felt the blood freeze in his veins, as if he’d been stabbed over and over. Every word was a betrayal. Every glance, a lie. He felt used, deceived more alone than ever before.
At dawn, Ash returned to Mary, his face marked by exhaustion and heartbreak. “Mary… you were right. Lexy lied to me. He lied to everyone.”
Mary embraced him tightly, tears streaming down her face. “It doesn’t matter what happened. We’re together now. Together, we’ll protect Nyfurion.”
Ash looked into her eyes, his voice trembling but resolute. “Forgive me. I doubted you doubted us. But now I know who I am. And I know that without you, my path would’ve been very different.”
Mary smiled through her tears. “You’re not alone, Ash. You never will be.”
They clasped hands, vowing to face Lexy together united by love and courage. The fate of Nyfurion was in their hands.

en.title: The Rise of the King
paras: Night fell over Nyfurion like an omen. No one expected the storm to arrive so swiftly. A thunderous roar shattered the silence the castle walls trembled, and the torches extinguished one by one. From the shadows emerged Lexy, surrounded by his followers, eyes burning with hatred and power. The dark magic he had honed during his years of exile coiled around his hands like black flames.

Mary and Ash were caught off guard. The screams of the townspeople mingled with the thunder of magical blasts raining down on the walls. Shadow creatures poured into the corridors, spreading terror. The floor shook, windows shattered into a thousand shards, and the sky above the castle split with black lightning that seemed to tear the night itself apart.

Ash grabbed Mary’s hand, holding it tightly. Their eyes met for a moment filled with fear, but also with resolve. Mary (whispering): “Don’t leave me, Ash. Whatever happens, we stay together.” Ash: “I’ll never leave you.”

Ash charged through the invaded halls, cutting through the darkness with his radiant magic. Every step was a battle Lexy’s followers attacked without mercy, but Ash held his ground, driven by hope and his love for Mary. The corridors became warzones: statues crumbled, tapestries caught fire, and screams echoed through the ancient stone.

In the heart of the castle, among shattered columns and broken stained glass, Ash came face to face with Lexy. The old mage stared at him with a gaze both paternal and cruel, his figure cloaked in a pulsing aura of darkness. Lexy: “At last, Ash. Your destiny is here. Join me, and Nyfurion will be ours. Together, no one can stop us.” Ash: “You lied to me for years. You used me. I’ll never be like you.” Lexy (coldly smiling): “I gave you everything! Without me, you’d still be an orphan in the shadows. Don’t you see? Power is all that matters! Look at what you can do what you can become!” Ash: “Power without love is only destruction. And I choose to protect, not to rule.”

A flash of rage crossed Lexy’s face. In an instant, the throne room was swallowed by a vortex of dark magic: slick shadows coiled like serpents around the columns, slithering across the walls and choking the torchlight. The air turned icy, charged with electricity and dread. The cries of lost souls echoed through the stone as the floor cracked beneath Ash’s feet, revealing chasms of pure darkness.

Ash was struck by a shockwave his body hurled against a column, blood streaking down his forehead. Every blow from Lexy was a wound, but also a memory: the loneliness of childhood, the fear of being no one, the hope Mary had given him. He rose, staggering, breath ragged—but his gaze was unwavering.

Lexy’s voice thundered through the chamber: “You’re weak! Your heart will betray you! Look how they tremble, how they beg for mercy. Only those who rule through fear can ever be truly free!” Ash, gritting his teeth, stood tall. He was torn, his hands shaking, but in his eyes burned a new light. “My heart is my strength. And I am not alone.”

The duel grew fiercer. Lexy raised his arms, and shards of black ice rained from the ceiling as gales of freezing wind swept the hall. From his hands burst shadow beasts creatures with red eyes and razor claws lunging at Ash. With a desperate gesture, Ash summoned a shield of light that exploded into a thousand sparks, repelling the creatures and briefly illuminating the terrified faces of the townspeople hiding behind the columns.

The floor split into deep crevices, ancient pillars collapsed with thunderous crashes, and the battle spilled into ruined chambers and rain-lashed terraces. Fire clashed with ice Lexy’s magic was a vortex of hatred and despair, while Ash’s was pure, fueled by love for Mary and the hope of the people.

Lexy, voice ragged with fury, screamed: “No one can stop me! I’ve seen the darkness beyond darkness. I’ve made pacts with the shadows themselves!” Ash, gasping, turned to Mary, who looked at him with tearful, courageous eyes. “You’re just a man blinded by fear. And I’m not afraid of you anymore.”

In a fit of desperation, Lexy raised his hands to the sky, unleashing a vortex of dark energy upon the relics hidden in the castle’s heart. The walls trembled, stained glass shattered in a rain of crystal, and an inhuman scream tore through the air.

Lexy, enraged, unleashed a wave of dark magic that hurled Ash against a column. Bones cracked, blood ran down his face. Lexy gave him no respite he summoned chains of shadow that wrapped around Ash’s arms, tightening until he screamed in pain.

Ash broke free with a violent pull the chains dissolved into smoke. He lunged at Lexy, and the two tumbled to the ground amid the rubble, trading punches and blows. Ash tasted blood in his mouth as Lexy struck his face with unnatural strength, fueled by dark magic. “Surrender!” Lexy roared, his icy hand tightening around Ash’s throat. “You can’t win!” With his last strength, Ash struck Lexy in the stomach, breaking free. They staggered to their feet, clothes torn, faces bloodied and bruised. Lexy hurled a volley of shadow darts that pierced Ash’s shoulder, drawing a cry of pain. The agony was searing but Ash did not yield.
The people, hidden among the ruins, watched the scene in stunned silence. Mary cried out Ash’s name, tears in her eyes.
Lexy raised his hands, ready to strike the final blow. “Goodbye, Ash!”

But just when all seemed lost, Ash heard Mary’s voice and felt the warmth of hope. He gathered every fragment of light left within him. His body trembled, his hands bloodied. He rose, eyes blazing with a new light. “It won’t end like this!” he shouted, and with a cry, unleashed all his energy.

His hands shone like twin suns, and a blinding explosion of white light engulfed the hall. Lexy was struck head-on the shadows screamed, twisted, and dissolved one by one. Lexy’s body crumbled into a storm of ash and wind, and the dark magic vanished forever.

The silence that followed was unreal. The hall lay in ruins, Ash’s blood stained the stone, but light streamed through the shattered windows, brushing the faces of the trembling townspeople emerging from their hiding places. Ash, wounded but standing, looked out at the gathered crowd. All eyes were on him for the first time, they saw not just a boy, but a true king.
Mary ran to him, tears streaming down her face, blending with a smile of pure joy. Ash held her close, breath still ragged, blood dripping from his temple.
The elders of the castle, still trembling, knelt before Ash. No one had ever brought such light to those ancient walls. From that day forward, Nyfurion had its first true king.

Peace returned. Ash and Mary were crowned king and queen in a ceremony that united the entire kingdom. The magical relics, now more precious than ever, were sealed in secret chambers, protected by enchantments known only to them. No one would ever again use them for darkness.

The people celebrated Nyfurion’s rebirth with a festival that lasted for days. The streets filled with music, dancing, and color. Children ran between the stalls, and the elders told the tale of the night when light defeated shadow. Ash and Mary, bound by love and truth, vowed to protect the kingdom forever.

And so, within walls that had once known pain and betrayal, a new era of hope was born led by a king and queen who had chosen the light, even when all seemed lost. Nyfurion, at last, knew peace again.

That night, returning to the castle, Ash felt a new resolve awaken within him. He would not let solitude define him. He would uncover every mystery of Nyfurion, protect its people, and honor the memory of a family he never knew. From that day on, the orphaned boy began to grow faster, driven by the desire to find his place in the world—and by the suspicion that his fate was entwined with Lexy’s and the medallion’s.

it.title: The Awakening
paras: The years passed quietly within the walls of Nyfurion’s castle. Ash, now a teenager, had changed: the lonely child had become a sharp-eyed young man, restless in spirit and driven by a growing desire to uncover his origins a fire within him that refused to die.

Questions crowded his mind: Who were his parents, truly? Why had they left him at the castle gates? And why did no one seem willing to speak of his past? The more he searched for answers in the castle’s corridors, the more he encountered silence and evasive glances. At times, Ash felt as though everyone knew something he didn’t and that made him feel even more alone.

Only Lexy seemed willing to share fragments of truth. Ash often visited the old man’s hut at the edge of the forest, where the air smelled of moss and mystery. Lexy taught him to read ancient symbols, to recognize the marks left by time on stones and trees, to sense the invisible magic flowing through the kingdom. In those hours, Ash felt truly seen as if Lexy perceived something in him that no one else could. Ash listened intently to every word, every tale about Nyfurion’s relics. He sensed that behind those stories lay something vital, perhaps the key to understanding his destiny. But Lexy was skilled at changing the subject when Ash’s questions became too direct, leaving him with a growing frustration and an even deeper curiosity. Sometimes, the old man would fall silent mid-sentence, as if afraid of revealing too much, and his gaze would suddenly darken.

As the months passed, Ash realized he was changing on the inside too. A new strength was awakening within him a heightened sensitivity to the world around him. His dreams grew more vivid, filled with symbols and visions from ancient times. He often woke in the middle of the night, heart pounding, convinced he had glimpsed answers in his sleep. Each night, before drifting off, he promised himself that one day he would uncover the full truth about his origins and the mystery surrounding Nyfurion’s relics.

During the day, Ash continued to move between the castle halls and the surrounding villages. In the castle, he observed carefully, trying to catch fragments of conversations that might reveal something about his past. He often retreated to the library, poring over dusty old tomes in search of symbols like those Lexy had shown him. He began to notice details he’d missed before: a medallion like Lexy’s in an ancient fresco, a phrase in an unknown language carved into a column, a hidden symbol tucked between the pages of an old book.

One evening, while in the map room, Ash noticed a candle flame flicker strangely as he passed. He stopped, intrigued, and reached toward the light. Without knowing how, the flame stretched toward him, dancing in the air as if responding to his presence. Ash pulled his hand back, startled, heart racing. No one seemed to notice but he knew something extraordinary had just occurred.
The next day, he returned to Lexy in the forest, determined to share what had happened. The old man greeted him with a watchful gaze.
“Lexy, yesterday… something strange happened. A candle it moved toward me. I didn’t touch it, but it was like it heard me.”

Lexy paused for a moment, then offered a faint smile. “Do not fear, Ash. The ancient blood within you is beginning to awaken. The stories I tell you are not merely echoes of the past they are keys to unlock doors within yourself.”
Ash stared at him, confused and fascinated. “What do you mean, Lexy?”
Lexy replied, “Your powers belong only to those who bear the mark of Nyfurion’s dynasty. Your strength is still raw, but it will grow. You must learn to listen to it.”

From that day on, Ash began to train in secret. He practiced moving small objects, sensing the presence of people without seeing them, feeling the heartbeat of nature around him. Each time he succeeded even for a moment he felt a deep joy and a subtle fear. He knew these powers made him different, but also that they were the key to discovering who he truly was.

In the castle, his movements became more deliberate. He studied the symbols carved into doors, the ancient armor lining the corridors, the paintings of kings and queens with stern faces. He began to notice details he’d once overlooked: a medallion like Lexy’s in a faded fresco, a phrase in an unknown tongue etched into a column.
One evening, as Lexy showed him an ancient manuscript, Ash asked, “Why does no one ever speak of the relics? Why does everyone seem afraid of these stories?”

Lexy looked at him for a long moment, then answered in a low voice, “Because power, Ash, frightens those who do not understand it. And those who crave it are often willing to do anything to possess it. You must be different. You must learn to know your strength but also to protect it.”

Those words etched themselves into Ash’s mind. From that moment on, each day became a discovery of himself, of the kingdom, and of the secrets that surrounded him. And each night, in his dreams, Lexy’s voice and the call of the relics grew stronger and more urgent.

it.title: Bonds and Power
paras: As the years passed, the bond between Ash and Lexy grew ever stronger. What had begun as mere curiosity had deepened into something profound built on trust, respect, and affection. Lexy had become Ash’s confidant, his guide, and perhaps the father figure he had never known. And Ash, in turn, brought a new light into Lexy’s life a hope the old man had long thought lost.

Lexy, who had once known both glory and disgrace within the castle walls, saw in Ash a chance for redemption. Day after day, in their secret meetings, Lexy shared stories of ancient magic and the relics of Nyfurion. Ash listened intently, absorbing every word, every gesture, every tale Lexy passed on with patience and care. Between them, a language had formed one of glances and silences, of small gestures that spoke louder than words.

Ash’s power grew alongside their bond. His abilities sharpened: he could sense people from far away, hear their deepest thoughts, influence wind and rain with sheer will. Lexy urged him to push his limits. “Listen to the breath of the forest, Ash. Feel how magic flows beneath the bark of the trees, through the roots and leaves.” Ash would close his eyes and let the world around him transform into a mosaic of ancient energies and forgotten sounds.

But with growth came new challenges. The stronger his magic became, the harder it was to contain. A surge of emotion anger, fear, sorrow could trigger inexplicable phenomena: a sudden storm, a flash of light in his hands, a whisper that made the earth tremble. One night, overwhelmed by anxiety, Ash unintentionally withered every rose in the royal garden.

At the castle, no one suspected a thing. Ash had learned to hide every trace of his powers, to behave like any other quiet, respectful young man. The nobles saw him as reserved perhaps a little strange but nothing more. Only Lexy knew the truth: behind that mask was the future of Nyfurion, the heir to an ancient bloodline, destined to reshape the kingdom’s fate.

Ash trusted Lexy completely. He had nothing to fear or so he believed. He could not imagine that behind the mask of affection and wisdom lay a darker plan. Lexy needed him. He knew Ash descended from a powerful family the last survivor after the bloodline was wiped out in a surprise attack. Only Lexy had seen the truth, recognizing in Ash the signs of royal lineage. That was why he had drawn close to him, binding him tightly, guiding him step by step toward the discovery of his hidden power.

But Lexy’s true purpose was far from what Ash could have imagined: he intended to use the boy’s strength for revenge to destroy Nyfurion and punish the kingdom that had exiled him. And while Ash surrendered to trust, unaware, the fate of Nyfurion crept ever closer to a dark turning point.

it.title: An Unexpected Encounter
paras: It was a clear evening as Ash made his way back to the castle after one of his usual meetings with Lexy. His mind was still full of thoughts and questions, his steps quick along the paths that cut through the forest and meadows. The air smelled of damp earth and leaves, and the birdsong mingled with the rustling wind in the branches. He expected nothing unusual from the day yet fate had a surprise in store.

As he walked alongside a small stream, Ash heard a rustle in the bushes. Before he could turn, something or rather, someone collided with him, nearly knocking him over. A startled exclamation, then a crystalline laugh: “Oh, sorry! I didn’t see you!”

Ash found himself on the ground, still dazed. In front of him, a girl with copper-colored hair had gotten her dress tangled in the branches. She tried to free herself, but the more she struggled, the more comical the situation became. Ash, still a bit stunned, couldn’t help but laugh.

“Let me help you,” he said, offering his hand. The girl accepted, but as she tried to stand, she slipped again, pulling Ash down with her. The two ended up sitting in the grass, side by side, cheeks flushed from laughter.
“My name’s Mary,” she said, still catching her breath. “And you must be Ash, right? I’ve heard about you at the castle… though I didn’t expect you to be so… um, agile!”
Ash laughed, feeling a lightness he hadn’t felt in a long time. “I’m usually more careful, but today fate decided to test me.”
Mary smiled, her gaze shining with a light all its own. “Then we’re both in the same boat. I’m new around here too. Got lost in the paths and… well, you know the rest.”

They stood up together, still laughing, and Ash offered to walk her back to the castle. They strolled side by side, exchanging jokes and stories as if they’d known each other forever. Mary spoke of how she had recently moved to Nyfurion, how she found the woods enchanting and the castle’s ancient walls mysterious. Ash, in turn, told her about his favorite places, the nights spent watching stars from the highest towers, and the stories he’d learned from the village elders.

With each step, the conversation grew more natural. Mary had a contagious laugh and a way of seeing the world that intrigued Ash. “You know,” she said at one point, “I think the best things happen when you get lost. Like today.”
Ash nodded, feeling a strange happiness rise within him. “Maybe fate made us stumble into each other for a reason.”

As they crossed a small wooden bridge, Mary paused to look at the sunset’s reflection on the water. “I didn’t expect Nyfurion to be so beautiful. Maybe, with the right company, everything feels more magical.”
Ash watched her in silence, struck by her sincerity. “Sometimes it takes very little to change a day. Or maybe an entire life.”

By the time they reached the castle gates, the sun was low on the horizon and the towers cast long shadows across the fields. Before parting, Mary turned to Ash and smiled once more. “I hope I get lost again maybe with you next time.”

Ash watched her walk away, his heart light and his mind full of new questions. That encounter, born of chance and a small accident, marked the beginning of something special a spark that would forever alter both their destinies. And as the sun set behind Nyfurion’s towers, Ash felt, for the first time, that the future no longer frightened him.

it.title: Shadows Between Feelings
paras: After their first encounter, Ash and Mary began seeing each other more and more often. At first, it was just chance meetings in the castle gardens, strolls through the village alleys, or quiet conversations beneath the stars. Mary brought a lightness into Ash’s life that he had never known before with her, he laughed, opened up, and finally felt free to be himself. With each passing day, their bond grew deeper, and Ash found himself longing more and more for her presence.

Over time, their meetings became a cherished ritual. Mary was the only one who could make Ash forget the weight of his responsibilities and the shadows that followed him. Together, they explored hidden corners of the kingdom, shared dreams and fears, and between them blossomed a sincere connection built on small gestures and knowing glances. Ash felt truly alive, as if beside Mary he could finally be the boy he had always wished to be.

Their days were filled with laughter and confidences, with spontaneous games in the courtyards and long conversations under the moonlight. Mary had a gift for sensing Ash’s thoughts even when he remained silent, and often a single look was enough to understand each other. Ash, in turn, found himself sharing secrets he had never told anyone not even himself.

And yet, despite the happiness Mary gave him, Ash couldn’t escape Lexy’s influence. The old man continued to meet with him, spinning tales of vengeance and power, pushing him toward a destiny that felt heavier with each passing day. Lexy was skilled at weaving truth with lies, exploiting Ash’s insecurities and his longing to uncover his origins. Every time Ash returned from one of these meetings, he felt a strange unease inside him as if a part of him was drifting away from the light Mary had brought into his life.

As the years went by, Mary began to notice changes in Ash. His gaze grew darker, his silences longer. She often found him lost in thought, distant even when he was right beside her. Ash was becoming more powerful but also more troubled, as if an inner battle was consuming him day by day. Sometimes, during their walks, Mary would see him staring into nothingness, fists clenched, as if fighting an invisible war.

Mary tried to reach him, to pull him back to reality, but Ash seemed to slip away trapped by a promise he had made to himself and to Lexy. “Ash, what’s tormenting you?” she would ask at times, but he would only offer a faint smile, change the subject, or retreat into silence.

One day, during a storm, Mary found Ash in the forest, kneeling before an ancient tree, his hands trembling with energy. Lightning lit up the sky and rain poured down, but Mary didn’t hesitate. She knelt beside him, unfazed by the mud and cold, and took his hands in hers. “Ash, what’s happening to you?” she whispered, her voice trembling with worry.

Ash looked at her with eyes full of pain and confusion, unable to find the words. He felt the magic boiling inside him, out of control, as if something dark was trying to take over. “I don’t know, Mary… I feel like I’m losing myself. I’m afraid of what I’m becoming.”

Mary held him tightly, wrapping him in an embrace as if trying to shield him from the entire world. “You’re not alone, Ash. I’m here. Don’t let the darkness take you. Whatever happens, we’ll fight together.”

In that moment, Mary understood that something dark was growing inside him and that only the truth could save him. She resolved to do whatever it took to bring Ash back to the light, even if it meant facing the shadows that threatened to tear them apart forever.

it.title: The Truth Revealed
paras: The kingdom of Nyfurion seemed wrapped in an eerie calm. Days passed quietly within the castle walls, yet Mary sensed a subtle unease drifting through the air. Ash had changed his eyes, once full of curiosity, now often stared into nothingness. He wandered the corridors with a tense expression, fists clenched, as if fighting an invisible war.

Mary watched him from afar, her heart tight with worry. She saw him gaze silently into the fireplace, or roam the halls at night, unable to sleep. Every time she tried to ask what tormented him, Ash withdrew into stubborn silence, avoiding her gaze.
Mary Begins to Investigate

One night, unable to bear the anguish any longer, Mary decided to act. She waited until the castle had fallen into silence, then slipped into the secret archives. Her fingers trembled as she flipped through ancient volumes, candlelight casting dancing shadows on the walls. Among the yellowed pages, she found familiar symbols the same ones she had seen in Ash’s dreams.

An old librarian caught her between the shelves. “Seeking answers, my lady?” Mary nodded, hesitant. “Tell me about Lexy. What is he hiding from his past?” The man lowered his gaze. “Lexy was exiled years ago. He sought power in forbidden relics. He was obsessed… and those who followed him paid dearly for his ambition.”

Mary thanked him with a nod and continued her search, listening to the whispers of an elderly woman who remembered the time of exile: “Lexy had stormy eyes and honeyed words. But his heart… his heart already belonged to the shadows.”
Discoveries and Suspicions

Digging through scrolls, Mary found a worn diary. Its pages told of a young Lexy brilliant, ambitious who had betrayed the kingdom’s trust in his thirst for power. In a flash, she saw the image of Lexy clutching a relic in his hands, his face twisted by greed.
Mary shuddered. It all made sense now: the symbols, the stories, Ash’s transformation. Lexy was the source of the darkness consuming the boy she loved.

That evening, Mary waited for Ash in the library, among the shadows of ancient shelves. Rain lashed against the windows, and the wind made the candles tremble. “Ash, we need to talk,” she said firmly, holding out the diary.

Ash looked at her, confused and defensive. “What is all this?” “It’s the truth about Lexy. He’s using you, Ash. He only wants to destroy the kingdom of Nyfurion. You are so much more than what he wants you to believe.”

Ash clenched his fists, his voice breaking. “Lexy has always protected me. He taught me everything. This can’t be true…” Mary stepped closer, her eyes filled with tears. “Can’t you see how much you’ve changed? You’re not yourself anymore. He’s pulling you away from me, from who you are.”
Ash turned away, torn between loyalty and doubt. “You don’t understand… I owe him everything.” “You don’t owe him your soul, Ash. You have to choose who you want to be.”
Ash ran off, heart in turmoil, but Mary’s words echoed in his mind like thunder.
Ash Discovers the Truth

That night, unable to find peace, Ash decided to follow Lexy. He moved silently through the village shadows, slipping past the castle walls and into the forest surrounding Nyfurion. His heart pounded as he hid among the trees, tracking the old man’s steps.
In a hidden clearing, lit only by the flickering glow of lanterns, Ash saw Lexy surrounded by armed men. Their voices were low, thick with hatred and hunger for power.
“Soon the kingdom will fall,” Lexy whispered to his followers. “Ash will do what he must. No one will suspect him until the time is right. Then Nyfurion will be ours.”
Ash felt the blood freeze in his veins, as if he’d been stabbed over and over. Every word was a betrayal. Every glance, a lie. He felt used, deceived more alone than ever before.
At dawn, Ash returned to Mary, his face marked by exhaustion and heartbreak. “Mary… you were right. Lexy lied to me. He lied to everyone.”
Mary embraced him tightly, tears streaming down her face. “It doesn’t matter what happened. We’re together now. Together, we’ll protect Nyfurion.”
Ash looked into her eyes, his voice trembling but resolute. “Forgive me. I doubted you doubted us. But now I know who I am. And I know that without you, my path would’ve been very different.”
Mary smiled through her tears. “You’re not alone, Ash. You never will be.”
They clasped hands, vowing to face Lexy together united by love and courage. The fate of Nyfurion was in their hands.

it.title: The Rise of the King
paras: Night fell over Nyfurion like an omen. No one expected the storm to arrive so swiftly. A thunderous roar shattered the silence the castle walls trembled, and the torches extinguished one by one. From the shadows emerged Lexy, surrounded by his followers, eyes burning with hatred and power. The dark magic he had honed during his years of exile coiled around his hands like black flames.

Mary and Ash were caught off guard. The screams of the townspeople mingled with the thunder of magical blasts raining down on the walls. Shadow creatures poured into the corridors, spreading terror. The floor shook, windows shattered into a thousand shards, and the sky above the castle split with black lightning that seemed to tear the night itself apart.

Ash grabbed Mary’s hand, holding it tightly. Their eyes met for a moment filled with fear, but also with resolve. Mary (whispering): “Don’t leave me, Ash. Whatever happens, we stay together.” Ash: “I’ll never leave you.”

Ash charged through the invaded halls, cutting through the darkness with his radiant magic. Every step was a battle Lexy’s followers attacked without mercy, but Ash held his ground, driven by hope and his love for Mary. The corridors became warzones: statues crumbled, tapestries caught fire, and screams echoed through the ancient stone.

In the heart of the castle, among shattered columns and broken stained glass, Ash came face to face with Lexy. The old mage stared at him with a gaze both paternal and cruel, his figure cloaked in a pulsing aura of darkness. Lexy: “At last, Ash. Your destiny is here. Join me, and Nyfurion will be ours. Together, no one can stop us.” Ash: “You lied to me for years. You used me. I’ll never be like you.” Lexy (coldly smiling): “I gave you everything! Without me, you’d still be an orphan in the shadows. Don’t you see? Power is all that matters! Look at what you can do what you can become!” Ash: “Power without love is only destruction. And I choose to protect, not to rule.”

A flash of rage crossed Lexy’s face. In an instant, the throne room was swallowed by a vortex of dark magic: slick shadows coiled like serpents around the columns, slithering across the walls and choking the torchlight. The air turned icy, charged with electricity and dread. The cries of lost souls echoed through the stone as the floor cracked beneath Ash’s feet, revealing chasms of pure darkness.

Ash was struck by a shockwave his body hurled against a column, blood streaking down his forehead. Every blow from Lexy was a wound, but also a memory: the loneliness of childhood, the fear of being no one, the hope Mary had given him. He rose, staggering, breath ragged—but his gaze was unwavering.

Lexy’s voice thundered through the chamber: “You’re weak! Your heart will betray you! Look how they tremble, how they beg for mercy. Only those who rule through fear can ever be truly free!” Ash, gritting his teeth, stood tall. He was torn, his hands shaking, but in his eyes burned a new light. “My heart is my strength. And I am not alone.”

The duel grew fiercer. Lexy raised his arms, and shards of black ice rained from the ceiling as gales of freezing wind swept the hall. From his hands burst shadow beasts creatures with red eyes and razor claws lunging at Ash. With a desperate gesture, Ash summoned a shield of light that exploded into a thousand sparks, repelling the creatures and briefly illuminating the terrified faces of the townspeople hiding behind the columns.

The floor split into deep crevices, ancient pillars collapsed with thunderous crashes, and the battle spilled into ruined chambers and rain-lashed terraces. Fire clashed with ice Lexy’s magic was a vortex of hatred and despair, while Ash’s was pure, fueled by love for Mary and the hope of the people.

Lexy, voice ragged with fury, screamed: “No one can stop me! I’ve seen the darkness beyond darkness. I’ve made pacts with the shadows themselves!” Ash, gasping, turned to Mary, who looked at him with tearful, courageous eyes. “You’re just a man blinded by fear. And I’m not afraid of you anymore.”

In a fit of desperation, Lexy raised his hands to the sky, unleashing a vortex of dark energy upon the relics hidden in the castle’s heart. The walls trembled, stained glass shattered in a rain of crystal, and an inhuman scream tore through the air.

Lexy, enraged, unleashed a wave of dark magic that hurled Ash against a column. Bones cracked, blood ran down his face. Lexy gave him no respite he summoned chains of shadow that wrapped around Ash’s arms, tightening until he screamed in pain.

Ash broke free with a violent pull the chains dissolved into smoke. He lunged at Lexy, and the two tumbled to the ground amid the rubble, trading punches and blows. Ash tasted blood in his mouth as Lexy struck his face with unnatural strength, fueled by dark magic. “Surrender!” Lexy roared, his icy hand tightening around Ash’s throat. “You can’t win!” With his last strength, Ash struck Lexy in the stomach, breaking free. They staggered to their feet, clothes torn, faces bloodied and bruised. Lexy hurled a volley of shadow darts that pierced Ash’s shoulder, drawing a cry of pain. The agony was searing but Ash did not yield.
The people, hidden among the ruins, watched the scene in stunned silence. Mary cried out Ash’s name, tears in her eyes.
Lexy raised his hands, ready to strike the final blow. “Goodbye, Ash!”

But just when all seemed lost, Ash heard Mary’s voice and felt the warmth of hope. He gathered every fragment of light left within him. His body trembled, his hands bloodied. He rose, eyes blazing with a new light. “It won’t end like this!” he shouted, and with a cry, unleashed all his energy.

His hands shone like twin suns, and a blinding explosion of white light engulfed the hall. Lexy was struck head-on the shadows screamed, twisted, and dissolved one by one. Lexy’s body crumbled into a storm of ash and wind, and the dark magic vanished forever.

The silence that followed was unreal. The hall lay in ruins, Ash’s blood stained the stone, but light streamed through the shattered windows, brushing the faces of the trembling townspeople emerging from their hiding places. Ash, wounded but standing, looked out at the gathered crowd. All eyes were on him for the first time, they saw not just a boy, but a true king.
Mary ran to him, tears streaming down her face, blending with a smile of pure joy. Ash held her close, breath still ragged, blood dripping from his temple.
The elders of the castle, still trembling, knelt before Ash. No one had ever brought such light to those ancient walls. From that day forward, Nyfurion had its first true king.

Peace returned. Ash and Mary were crowned king and queen in a ceremony that united the entire kingdom. The magical relics, now more precious than ever, were sealed in secret chambers, protected by enchantments known only to them. No one would ever again use them for darkness.

The people celebrated Nyfurion’s rebirth with a festival that lasted for days. The streets filled with music, dancing, and color. Children ran between the stalls, and the elders told the tale of the night when light defeated shadow. Ash and Mary, bound by love and truth, vowed to protect the kingdom forever.

And so, within walls that had once known pain and betrayal, a new era of hope was born led by a king and queen who had chosen the light, even when all seemed lost. Nyfurion, at last, knew peace again.
